Primitive fourth-root eigenbasis exists in every such finite field; each nonempty support has exactly (q−1)^{|I|−1} projective classes, Frobenius orbit e(I)=4/gcd(4,I−I). Right nucleus follows from fg−gf and the known right-nucleus/eigenring characterization, yielding 16/r(I). All automorphisms follow from [2] n≥m−1 and exactly N lifts per stabilizing exponent, hence 4N/e(I). The 15 nonempty supports minus {0} partition into five pair groups and give precise polynomial counts. Reproduced by two independent exact enumerators for q=5,9,13,17, with auxiliary q=7 n6. Finite checks supplement, not substitute for, the symbolic exhaustive support proof.

originality.rationale: Target is the exact five-row *joint frequency distribution* by right-nucleus F-dimension and full F-automorphism-group order in the smallest composite extension degree. Nevins--Pumplün supplies an explicit classification of individual isomorphism classes but no such joint frequency table. Brown--Pumplün characterizes automorphisms, without stratifying isomorphism classes jointly with nuclei; Pumplün determines right nuclei, without an automorphism-order census. Independent support enumeration integrates these inputs and derives new exact polynomial multiplicities and the invariant-incomparability phenomenon. This is not claiming new foundational classifications or priority of the unstratified total. No directly covering joint table found. Historical priority and elementary derivability from the combined structural inputs remain live risks.

value.rationale: Right nucleus size and automorphism-group order are standard intrinsic invariants in nonassociative cyclic algebras and are not functionally dependent in composite degree. Degree four is the smallest composite cyclic extension, where nontrivial intermediate coefficient subfields make the nucleus variable; the table completely counts every F-isomorphism class by both natural invariants for every q≡1 mod4, including zero-divisor algebras, and exhibits sharp independence between the invariants. These are exact arithmetic classifications, not an arbitrary numerical slice. General or division-only applications remain outside the claim.
